references.text: Job experienced similar losses of oxen, donkeys, and sheep to enemies and robbers, illustrating the curse described in Deuteronomy.
The same warning that enemies will eat what you sow and work for, as part of the covenant curses.
A parallel curse in Leviticus about not being satisfied with your food, reflecting the loss of the ox you cannot eat.
Amos prophesies similar losses where what you work for is taken away and given to others.
The book of Micah describes how one sows but does not harvest, presses olives but does not anoint oneself with oil—the same theme of deprived fruit.
Zephaniah prophesies that houses will be built but not inhabited, vineyards planted but wine not drunk—the same curse pattern.
The Midianites took the Israelites' livestock and destroyed their crops, a direct fulfillment of this curse in the time of the Judges.
